conflicts.description: The official LE physical switch-location drawing marks the disputed upper-right-orbit coordinate as switch 61, while the same manual's switch matrix grid identifies switch 58 as RIGHT ORBIT and the known-working LE VPX script drives sw58 without a sw61 handler. The address mapping cannot be reconciled without guessing, so both spatial placements and the unused classification for 61 are withheld.

mechanisms.behavior: The 6-ball physical trough uses position sensors 17-22 and jam sensor 23. The working script initializes 6 balls and output 1 ejects from the right end.
mechanisms.label: 6-ball trough

mechanisms.behavior: Output 2 fires a ball at dedicated D15/public 86. The working script uses a 0.6-second impulse and power 62 with 0.3 randomness as a proven baseline.
mechanisms.label: Auto launcher

mechanisms.behavior: A ball rests on switch 62 until output 5 ejects it. The working script uses angle 25, force 16, and route variance.
mechanisms.label: Hulk eject

mechanisms.behavior: Switches 52-55 stay down independently. Public auxiliary output 51, physical driver 41 resets all four targets.
mechanisms.label: HULK four-drop bank

mechanisms.behavior: Outputs 3 and 4 drive opposite Hulk rotation directions. Wheel optos 41 and 42 report indexed motion; stop each drive at the intended sensed position and never energize both directions together.
mechanisms.label: Rotating Hulk assembly

mechanisms.behavior: Public auxiliary output 56, physical driver 46 raises the Hulk arms while active and lowers them when released. The table animation moves from roughly 130 to 200 degrees in two-degree timer steps.
mechanisms.label: Hulk arm lift

mechanisms.behavior: Switch 57 reports a ball on the Hulk platter. Public auxiliary output 54, physical driver 44 energizes the magnet; the working table uses radius 16 and does not force the ball to center.
mechanisms.label: Hulk platter magnet

mechanisms.behavior: Three active-low optos are initialized high when empty and fall low as balls occupy positions bottom-to-top. Output 12 drops the retaining post/releases locked balls.
mechanisms.label: Three-ball Loki lock

mechanisms.behavior: The playfield ball physically spins the Tesseract; it has no controller motor. Opposed optos 45 and 46 pulse as the inertial wheel crosses their positions. Preserve free rotation, collision-derived angular velocity, and gradual drag.
mechanisms.label: Inertial Tesseract spinner

mechanisms.behavior: Left, right, and bottom pop switches 30-32 directly correspond to outputs 9-11; the shared pop flasher is output 25.
mechanisms.label: Three pop bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Slingshot switches 26/27 drive outputs 13/14 and share flasher output 20.
mechanisms.label: Left and right slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: The two lower flippers use outputs 15/16, dedicated cabinet buttons D9/D11, and normally-closed EOS contacts D10/D12. Preserve SAM fast-flip behavior.
mechanisms.label: Lower flipper pair

mechanisms.behavior: Switches 1-4 stay down independently and main output 6 resets the left THOR bank.
mechanisms.label: THOR four-drop bank

mechanisms.behavior: The bridge has down switch 8 and up switch 9. Output 22 supplies the motor and relay output 23 selects motion state; the working script treats 23 active as down (8 active, 9 clear) and inactive as up (8 clear, 9 active). Implement limit-switch cutoff in both directions.
mechanisms.label: Motorized bridge

mechanisms.behavior: Main output 7 opens the left orbit. Auxiliary public 57/physical 47 opens the right orbit. Auxiliary public 52/53, physical 42/43, actuate the right/left ramp gates. Each returns closed when its drive releases.
mechanisms.label: Orbit and ramp control gates

mechanisms.behavior: GI public address 0 is the common illumination channel. Main output 17 and auxiliary public outputs 55/58 switch the blue, green, and red 112-5033 LED supply rails shown on the LE GI location map. Keep the three relay channels distinct even if a table renderer also exposes a combined GI brightness.
mechanisms.label: RGB GI LED relay bank
